claims.statement: The Polish installed base is large, but storage-equipped prosumers are a substantially narrower initial segment.
Net-billing creates a real self-consumption and timing problem for households with flexible loads or storage.
The original monthly fee is material relative to the 2026 average G11 energy-supply denominator, so broad homeowner SaaS is not a conservative starting assumption.
SolarEdge already bundles the generic optimisation loop, including tariff and weather inputs, household production and consumption, batteries and controllable devices.
Commercial OEM API access cannot be assumed to be free or unrestricted; documented examples include rate limits, contracts, business-partner restrictions and usage billing.
Data Act user-directed sharing can help read access, but it does not itself authorise personal-data processing or remote control and permits proportionate security and trade-secret measures.
The paid control point must be a pre-specified, auditable installer decision and verification artifact, because generic forecasts and schedules are reproducible and already bundled.
Incremental household savings over OEM defaults and simple behavioural scheduling are not established.
Installer willingness to pay and the number of avoided visits or incremental retrofits per monitored site are not established.
Wholesaler distribution, OEM control rights and a path to 20000 paid sites remain unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: SolarEdge provides a bundled AI energy optimiser and homeowner control surface.
Fronius exposes professional monitoring and control-oriented data interfaces under its own commercial terms.
Average household consumption constrains the savings pool available to support a recurring fee.
The Data Act does not eliminate GDPR, security, trade-secret, firmware or warranty constraints.
Measurement standards make clear that a whole-site savings claim needs a defined baseline and boundary.
